rituals.hook: Error Trace — Catch the instant an unchosen thought begins.
rituals.rule: Feed Probe — Do not choose the content.
rituals.play: Data Check — Rest on one neutral point. When a thought appears by itself, catch only its first instant before following it.
rituals.twist: Signal Scan — Classify only its form—word, image, memory, plan, sensation—then release.
rituals.reveal: Input Test — You notice an arrival before it becomes a complete thought.
rituals.mindBend: Error Scan — A thought can arrive before choice enters the room.
rituals.safety: Use only one ordinary thought. If forced mental blankness appears, stop and look at a physical object nearby.

rituals.hook: Glitch Read — Allow thought one but deny it a sequel.
rituals.rule: Frequency Scan — The first thought is permitted in full.
rituals.play: Waveform Read — Let one thought finish. For the next five seconds, any explanation, defence, prediction or replay counts as a sequel and gets no continuation.
rituals.twist: Pixel Check — A genuinely unrelated thought may enter.
rituals.reveal: Frame Probe — The original thought ends without becoming a chain.
rituals.mindBend: Feed Read — The first thought is not the loop.
rituals.safety: Keep this to everyday mental content. When compulsive thought monitoring appears, step out and move back to everyday activity.

rituals.safety: Choose everyday mental content. When greater thought preoccupation appears, end the round; do something simple and concrete.

rituals.hook: Echo Trace. Repeat the same item two different ways and compare what sticks.
rituals.rule: Orbit Check. One pair is massed; one pair is separated by distraction.
rituals.play: Pattern Check. Repeat MOON twice back-to-back. Then say RIVER once, count 1–5, and say RIVER again. Wait five seconds and notice which word returns more readily.
rituals.twist: Repeat Map. Do not rehearse either word during the final wait.
rituals.reveal: Pattern Replay. Spacing changes memory strength even though total repetitions are equal.
rituals.mindBend: Repeat Check. Identical material can leave different memory strength depending on spacing.
rituals.safety: Keep the round within material you can exit easily. If compulsive deeper searching shows up, step away from the exercise and focus on current external information.

rituals.play: Tension Ease — Make the whole scene flare white for a beat, then return to ordinary brightness.
rituals.twist: Load Release — No repeat.
rituals.reveal: Hold Soften — A visual state can be interrupted by a transient overexposure.
rituals.mindBend: Gravity Landing — Too much imagined light can briefly wash a scene toward whiteness.
rituals.safety: Use only a mild image or thought. Set the visual exercise aside if greater fear or vividness becomes noticeable; the round ends there.

rituals.mindBend: Tension Ease. Flattening light-dark differences makes boundaries less prominent without changing hue.
rituals.safety: Choose low-intensity content. If visual unreality or strain shows up, stop the exercise; stop editing the mental scene.

rituals.hook: Update Route. Make the thought obey two different rules instead of letting every part travel as certainty.
rituals.rule: Rebuild Path. Supported material gets smaller; inferred material must branch.

rituals.twist: Update Frame. Stop when you reach one statement that could actually be checked, asked, observed, or acted on.

rituals.play: Calm Centre: Before switching attention, encode the exact line, object, or action point with a simple mental marker.
rituals.twist: Quiet Anchor: Return using marker once.
rituals.reveal: Open Space: Attention can leave without losing its re-entry location.
rituals.mindBend: Steady Field: A concrete return cue preserves a route back to a task.
rituals.safety: Use only a low-effort attention sample. If compulsive focus checking appears, stop and allow attention to broaden or shift by itself.

rituals.hook: Restore Frame — Make competing explanations fight for the same pieces of evidence.
rituals.rule: Patch Frame — One observation cannot uniquely prove two different causes.
rituals.play: Stitch Map — Name the few actual observations behind the thought, then list more possible explanations than there are observations. Assign each explanation to the evidence it uses.
rituals.twist: Update Link — Find the first observation claimed by two different explanations. That collision means the evidence cannot distinguish between them.
rituals.reveal: Patch Route — The mind was treating shared evidence as if it uniquely selected one story.
rituals.mindBend: Stitch Path — When several explanations fit the same fact, confidence should shrink before the fact changes.
rituals.safety: For one pass, use harmless puzzle material. If self-judgment from frustration appears, stop the round; do something simple and everyday.

rituals.rule: Steady Point. Do not erase the dramatic item.
rituals.play: Soft Field. Choose one ordinary detail and hold it until it becomes clearer than the emotionally loud detail.
rituals.twist: Clear Field. Stop at crossover.
rituals.reveal: Still Point. Salience shifts while the underlying content stays unchanged.
rituals.mindBend: Gentle Pause. A neutral detail can overtake a dramatic one in attention pull without erasing either.
rituals.safety: For this round, choose comfortable visual attention. If compulsive focus checking appears, do not continue; return to a concrete task.

rituals.hook: Steady Pause. Let mental activity run without intervention.

rituals.twist: Still Space. Keep eyes open if that feels steadier.
rituals.reveal: Gentle Space. Mental activity continues for at least one moment without active management.

rituals.safety: For this round, choose quiet without forced blankness. If greater agitation or unreality appears, finish there and switch to external grounding.

rituals.twist: Frequency Scan — Do not complete the count during the observation window.
rituals.reveal: Waveform Read — An unfinished sequence creates a detectable pull toward closure.
rituals.mindBend: Pixel Check — An unfinished task can keep pulling after activity stops.
rituals.safety: Stay with brief mental observation for one pass. If detachment from ordinary activity develops, leave the round and return to your usual mental flow.

rituals.mindBend: Repair Route. Two equally vivid but unrelated mental items compete for mental version.
rituals.safety: Stay with comfortable visual attention. When compulsive focus checking becomes noticeable, stop and rejoin your normal activity.

rituals.hook: Interference Scan — Catch the easier question hiding inside the harder one.
rituals.rule: Noise Map — Write the hard question and the substitute question separately.

rituals.twist: Static Trace — Do not answer either question during the round.
rituals.reveal: Distortion Map — A hidden attribute substitution becomes visible before it can masquerade as the original judgement.
rituals.mindBend: Interference Trace — A hidden attribute substitution becomes visible before it can masquerade as the original judgement — hidden mechanism: detect when a difficult judgement is being answered by an easier substitute question and explicitly separate the two questions.
rituals.safety: Keep this to brief mental observation. When analysis of every mental event becomes noticeable, step out and shift attention outward.

rituals.safety: Use only mild, familiar sensations. If you realise needed medical assessment is being delayed, stop the ritual and seek that assessment rather than continuing to monitor the body.

rituals.safety: Use mild manageable material. When loss of present orientation appears, end it there and bring the situation to someone safe or clinical.

rituals.safety: Choose a small memory load for one pass. When compulsive rehearsal develops, end the round; record the item externally.

rituals.safety: Keep the round within simple real-world sensations. If the exercise shifts into dizziness or disorientation, leave the round and stop focusing and look around normally.

rituals.play: Rebuild Path — Set your current state as START and one useful near-term outcome as EXIT. Name the genuine blockers between them and the actions that are actually available.
rituals.twist: Rewire Link — Find the route with the fewest actions that never crosses a real blocker.
rituals.reveal: Update Frame — Feeling stuck can come from searching the whole maze when one short legal path already exists.
rituals.mindBend: Rebuild Frame — A blocked direct route does not mean there is no route.
rituals.safety: Stay with neutral examples for one pass. Do not continue if proof-seeking repetition develops; end the task without a personal rating.

rituals.mindBend: Patch Frame: Past time or money cannot improve the future value of continuing.
rituals.safety: Use one genuinely small action for this pass. When pushing through illness or exhaustion becomes noticeable, end it there and take a smaller practical action.

rituals.safety: Work only with a safe ordinary task. Rest or reassess the priority when the exercise shifts into pushing through illness or exhaustion; do not continue the task.

rituals.hook: Restore Map. Find out how many separate problems are really hiding inside the pile.
rituals.rule: Rewire Path. Only genuinely conflicting concerns need different colours.
rituals.play: Repair Link. Think of each active concern as a node. Draw a mental link only where two concerns compete for the same resource or decision. Assign colours so linked concerns never share one.
rituals.twist: Restore Path. Count the minimum colours needed rather than the number of concerns.
rituals.reveal: Rewire Route. Ten concerns may reduce to only a few distinct conflict systems.
rituals.mindBend: Repair Path. Overload often counts items; conflict mapping counts how many separate coordination problems actually exist.
rituals.safety: Keep this as a brief, low-stakes logic puzzle. If frustration becomes self-judgment or you start repeating the same search, stop and leave the colouring problem unfinished.

rituals.hook: Recalibration Pass: Lock one pleasant thing to one avoided task.
rituals.rule: Rewire Map: The pleasant item is available only while doing the target task.
rituals.play: Repair Route: Choose a harmless treat such as a favourite playlist. Mentally set the rule: playlist ON only while doing the first ten minutes of the avoided task; playlist OFF when the task stops.
rituals.twist: Restore Map: Do not give yourself the reward in advance.
rituals.reveal: Rewire Path: Task entry gains an immediate reward without requiring motivation to appear first.
rituals.mindBend: Repair Link: Making an immediate pleasure available only during a less-attractive task turns reward timing into a controllable contingency that supports engagement.
rituals.safety: Limit this to one genuinely small action. If compulsive productivity appears, do not continue; rest or reassess the priority.

rituals.hook: Rebuild Route — Find the felt halfway point of the episode without using a clock.
rituals.rule: Rewire Frame — No counting or breath timing.
rituals.play: Repair Frame — Let the thought or body alarm be present for a short manageable interval. Mark internally when you believe half the interval has passed.
rituals.twist: Recalibration Pass — After the interval ends, compare whether the first half felt longer or shorter than the second.
rituals.reveal: Rewire Map — Distress can distort the shape of time even when clock time does not change.
rituals.mindBend: Repair Route — A long-feeling moment is evidence about attention, not necessarily about duration or danger.
rituals.safety: Keep the interval brief and comfortable. If frustrating repetition develops, stop the exercise and return to ordinary activity.

rituals.hook: Rebuild Frame. Run facts and forecast side by side and catch the first drift.
rituals.rule: Rewire Point. A prediction step needs a matching evidence step to stay in sync.
rituals.play: Update Path. Imagine two tracks beginning together: WHAT IS KNOWN and WHAT I EXPECT NEXT. Advance them one step at a time.
rituals.twist: Rebuild Route. Mark the first moment the forecast moves ahead while the known-facts track has nothing new.
rituals.reveal: Rewire Frame. The future can feel synchronised with reality until the exact point prediction outruns evidence is made visible.
rituals.mindBend: Repair Frame. Worry often begins where two tracks that started together quietly stop moving at the same speed.
rituals.safety: Choose natural unforced breathing. When compulsive counting appears, end the round; let the pattern go.

rituals.hook: Gravity Settle: Turn a mental shape inside out without moving its outline.
rituals.rule: Burden Ease: The boundary cannot change.
rituals.play: Drag Reduction: Picture a simple closed loop. Treat the interior as 'outside' and everything around it as 'inside' for three beats.
rituals.twist: Strain Soften: Do not redraw or resize the loop.
rituals.reveal: Weight Lighten: Inside/outside assignment changes while the same boundary remains.
rituals.mindBend: Weight Shift: The inside and outside of a closed shape can trade roles while the boundary stays fixed.
rituals.safety: Use mildly charged content that stays easy to exit. If greater vividness or fear shows up, pause the exercise and return to what is physically in front of you.

rituals.hook: Rebuild Point — Put what happened and what it means in two slots, then swap them.
rituals.rule: Stitch Link — The labels travel with the content; fact status does not.
rituals.play: Update Route — Place the bare event in a left mental slot and your interpretation in a right slot. Hold both briefly, then swap their positions without changing either sentence.
rituals.twist: Rebuild Path — Notice whether the interpretation still feels like the 'fact slot' after the swap.
rituals.reveal: Rewire Link — Spatial position can expose how tightly an interpretation has fused with the event it follows.
rituals.mindBend: Update Frame — When fact and meaning live in one mental slot for too long, location can start masquerading as status.
rituals.safety: Use low-stakes material for one pass. If compulsive rehearsal develops, stop the round and release the items.

rituals.hook: Patch Point. Make yesterday's distractor become today's target.
rituals.rule: Stitch Point. One item is ignored first, then targeted.
rituals.play: Update Point. Trial 1: picture RED in blue ink and ignore the word RED while naming BLUE. Trial 2: immediately make RED the required response and notice any extra friction.
rituals.twist: Rebuild Point. Compare with a target that was not just ignored.
rituals.reveal: Stitch Link. A recently suppressed distractor can become temporarily harder to respond to when it turns into the target.
rituals.mindBend: Update Route. Prior holding back can linger: an item ignored moments earlier may become harder to select when it is promoted to target status.
rituals.safety: For this round, choose neutral examples. If proof-seeking repetition appears, do not continue; stop without grading how you did.

rituals.hook: Patch Route: Turn three separate mental items into one recoverable packet.

rituals.reveal: Stitch Point: Mental load can fall when related items are represented as one structure rather than three independent demands.
rituals.mindBend: Update Point: Working memory counts representations, not just facts.
rituals.safety: Use only low-stakes material. When compulsive rehearsal appears, stop and let a note carry the information.

rituals.hook: Signal Trace — Cross two words at their shared letter.
rituals.rule: Input Scan — The shared letter occupies one square only.
rituals.play: Error Check — Use CAT and MAP. Cross them at A, with CAT horizontal and MAP vertical, and hold the tiny word-cross for three beats.
rituals.twist: Interference Scan — Rotate the whole cross 90° without changing letter order inside either word.
rituals.reveal: Noise Map — Two verbal sequences share one spatial element while keeping separate directions.
rituals.mindBend: Signal Map — Two words can occupy perpendicular directions while sharing one letter.
rituals.safety: Make this a brief exercise with neutral examples for one pass. Stop without grading how you did if proof-seeking repetition develops; the round ends there.

rituals.hook: Patch Map. Ask one brutal question of the belief: was that detail actually in memory?
rituals.rule: Stitch Frame. Membership is YES or NO; plausibility does not count as remembered.
rituals.play: Restore Frame. Create a short set of details you genuinely remember from the event. Then take one claim from the current thought and test whether it was actually in that set.
rituals.twist: Patch Frame. If the answer is NO, move the claim from MEMORY to INFERENCE without deciding whether it is true or false.
rituals.reveal: Stitch Map. A plausible reconstruction can feel remembered even when it never entered the original memory set.
rituals.mindBend: Update Link. The brain can answer 'does this fit?' when the real question was 'was this actually there?'
rituals.safety: For this round, choose information safe to forget. If the exercise shifts into compulsive rehearsal, finish there and release the items.

rituals.safety: Restrict the exercise to one mild memory. If the exercise shifts into emotional flooding, stop the exercise; bring in trusted personal or clinical support.

rituals.safety: Keep this to a small memory load. If self-judgment from frustration appears, do not continue; capture the item in an external reminder.

rituals.hook: Rewire Route. Check whether the problem is truly accelerating or simply staying unpleasant.
rituals.rule: Repair Path. Judge changes between moments, not the moments alone.
rituals.play: Restore Route. Give the last four moments rough intensity numbers. Subtract adjacent values to get three changes, then compare those changes with one another.
rituals.twist: Patch Path. If the second differences are near zero, label the pattern STEADY rather than ACCELERATING.
rituals.reveal: Repair Map. A high level and a rising rate are different claims.
rituals.mindBend: Restore Point. The mind often reads sustained discomfort as escalation because it tracks magnitude but not the change in change.
rituals.safety: Choose low-stakes material. When repeated self-testing shows up, step out and place the information on paper or screen.

rituals.reveal: Repair Path: Working memory overload can be managed by explicit replacement rules instead of accidental accumulation.

rituals.safety: Limit this to low-stakes material. When self-judgment from frustration appears, leave the exercise; use an external note.

Data Check: The observations remain fixed while person and interpretation change roles.

Signal Scan: Imagine a tiny matrix: people on rows, possible meanings on columns. Notice where your current interpretation sits. Now transpose it so meanings become rows and people become columns.

TWIST
Input Test: Ask whether the same interpretation would be assigned as readily to another person with the same observable behaviour.

REVEAL
Error Scan: A social conclusion can depend on which axis the mind treats as fixed.

MIND BEND
Feed Check: Perspective bias often hides in the table layout: one person stays fixed while every negative meaning is allowed to move toward them.
rituals.thoughtEngineeringMechanism: Perspective transpose: represent people as rows and interpretations as columns, then swap the axes so each interpretation is tested across people rather than one person receiving every negative reading.

rituals.hook: Restore Path: See whether choosing a bundle creates extra variety.

rituals.mindBend: Repair Map: People may choose more variety when several future selections are made at once than when choosing day by day.

rituals.twist: Pressure Lower — Separate judgement of the decision from judgement of the outcome.

rituals.mindBend: Tension Drop — Chance can change moral blame even when intention, information and behaviour are identical.
rituals.safety: For one pass, use an open values question. If invalidation of grief becomes noticeable, stop the round; return to concrete reality.

rituals.hook: Channel Read — See whether your own choice quietly becomes your population estimate.

rituals.play: Frame Check — Choose tea or coffee. Then estimate, out of 100 random adults, how many would make the same choice. Notice whether your own preference pulls the estimate upward.
rituals.twist: Glitch Check — Keep the population estimate separate from whether your own choice is better.
rituals.reveal: Frequency Read — Personal preference and assumed social prevalence become distinct judgements.
rituals.mindBend: Channel Decode — Personal preference can inflate estimates of how many other people agree.
rituals.safety: Use a trivial preference with no social stakes. If the estimate starts feeding certainty about what other people think or becomes a self-worth comparison, stop and return to observable facts.

rituals.hook: Rebuild Point: Subtract what you actually observed from everything the thought is claiming.
rituals.rule: Stitch Link: The remainder is inference, not automatically error.
rituals.play: Update Route: Mentally list everything the thought says is true as set A. List only directly observed facts as set B. Remove every B item from A.
rituals.twist: Rebuild Path: Look at what remains and label it INFERENCE RESIDUE.
rituals.reveal: Rewire Link: A large conclusion can contain a much smaller factual core plus a sizeable interpretive remainder.
rituals.mindBend: Update Frame: Separating inference from fact does not require disproving the inference; subtraction alone changes its status.
rituals.safety: Use a low-stakes mental game. Move on without rating yourself when perfection pressure shows up; do not continue the task.

rituals.twist: Patch Link: If a broad self-story has no supporting middle layer, it cannot be placed.
rituals.reveal: Repair Pass: Overload can contain badly stacked abstraction rather than simply too many items.
rituals.mindBend: Restore Link: A large conclusion becomes unstable when it is balanced on a smaller fact than it can support.
rituals.safety: Use only neutral examples. If perfection pressure shows up, leave the round and move attention into a normal activity.

rituals.twist: Distortion Map: Do not add any extra sound between them.
rituals.reveal: Interference Trace: Three separate phonemes become one recognised word through temporal blending.

rituals.safety: Work only with manageable inner wording for one pass. If compulsive sentence repetition develops, stop the exercise; use external text as the reference.

rituals.hook: Stitch Map — Escape the current viewpoint with an L-shaped mental jump.
rituals.rule: Update Link — Change two dimensions in one direction and one in another.

rituals.twist: Stitch Path — Ask the same question from that new coordinate without returning through the intermediate viewpoints.
rituals.reveal: Update Map — A stuck thought can depend on remaining inside one local neighbourhood of perspective.
rituals.mindBend: Patch Point — Some viewpoints cannot be reached by a small straight shift; they require changing more than one dimension at once.
rituals.safety: Choose harmless puzzle material. If frustration turns into self-judgment, stop without rating your performance.

rituals.hook: Feed Check. Repeat a word until it starts sounding strangely like sound.
rituals.rule: Noise Filter. Use one neutral word and keep the pace steady.
rituals.play: Signal Trace. Pick the neutral word WINDOW. Repeat it internally around fifteen times at a quick, even pace. When the repetitions end, check whether the sound briefly feels stranger than its meaning.
rituals.twist: Input Scan. Avoid explaining the word while repeating it.
rituals.reveal: Error Check. A familiar word can momentarily feel like raw sound after sustained repetition.
rituals.mindBend: Interference Scan. Rapid repetition can make a familiar neutral word temporarily sound strange and less meaningful.
rituals.safety: Choose manageable inner wording. When compulsive sentence repetition becomes noticeable, step out and leave the sentence alone.

rituals.play: Repair Route — Imagine a clock. Point one hand toward the direction suggested by current facts and the other toward where the thought predicts things are heading.
rituals.twist: Restore Map — Estimate whether the angle is small, medium, or nearly opposite and ask what evidence would be needed to close it.
rituals.reveal: Rewire Path — A prediction can feel close to reality while pointing in a substantially different direction.
rituals.mindBend: Repair Link — The mind often measures certainty by vividness instead of by the angle between evidence and forecast.
rituals.safety: Use neutral examples. If self-judgment from frustration shows up, do not continue; switch tasks without keeping score.

rituals.hook: Rewire Point — Mirror the future against the past around NOW.

rituals.play: Rebuild Route — Build five slots: PAST-2 / PAST-1 / NOW / FUTURE-1 / FUTURE-2. Put the relevant memory and prediction pieces into matching positions.
rituals.twist: Rewire Frame — Check whether the future slots are merely mirrored versions of the past slots rather than independently supported forecasts.
rituals.reveal: Repair Frame — The future can look predicted when the mind has simply reflected an old sequence across the present.
rituals.mindBend: Recalibration Pass — A symmetrical story is psychologically elegant, but symmetry is not evidence that history will replay.
rituals.safety: Keep this to a brief comfortable pattern. If frustrating repetition appears, do not continue; let the pattern go.

rituals.hook: Distortion Trace. Ask what would happen if you actively changed the suspected cause.
rituals.rule: Interference Map. An intervention changes the candidate cause rather than merely observing it.
rituals.play: Frequency Check. Use a harmless example: coffee drinking and alertness rise together. Imagine actively setting coffee to zero while sleep and time of day stay the same. Ask what each causal story predicts.
rituals.twist: Channel Read. Do not treat correlation alone as the intervention result.
rituals.reveal: Static Scan. A causal claim becomes testable by what should change under deliberate intervention.
rituals.mindBend: Frame Check. INTERVENTION TEST reveals this: Two things moving together does not prove one caused the other.
rituals.safety: Use only a harmless, checkable claim. If real safety information is being dismissed, stop the thought experiment and verify the situation with an appropriate person or reliable source before continuing.

rituals.twist: Distortion Trace: Then apply the set rule: A includes all cases in B plus additional bank workers.

rituals.safety: Keep this to low-stakes examples. If real safety facts start being discounted, end the exercise and seek appropriate real-world verification or professional assessment rather than reasoning past those facts.

rituals.safety: Keep this to ordinary low-stakes evidence. When frightening unverifiable interpretations appear, step out and use external verification.

rituals.safety: Stay with neutral examples. When proof-seeking repetition becomes noticeable, stop and move on without forcing a solution.

rituals.hook: Update Map — Compress repeated mental runs into a tiny code.
rituals.rule: Patch Point — Consecutive repeats become one item plus a count.
rituals.play: Stitch Point — Watch the thought for repeated operations such as CHECK, WHY, REPLAY, PREDICT. When the same operation repeats, code it as 3×CHECK or 4×WHY instead of following every copy.
rituals.twist: Update Point — Reconstruct the original loop from the code and notice how much of its apparent length came from duplication.
rituals.reveal: Rebuild Point — A long rumination episode can contain very little unique cognitive content.
rituals.mindBend: Stitch Link — Compression exposes the difference between how long a loop lasts and how much information it contains.
rituals.safety: Keep this to a low-stakes mental game for one pass. When self-judgment from frustration develops, leave the exercise; switch to an ordinary activity.

rituals.safety: This is a shared-reality aid, not proof that everything is fine; if frightening uncertainty persists, show the same external information to a trusted person or clinician instead of checking it alone repeatedly.
